title: A peace accord at the Villa de la Unión ends the Uruguayan War
description: Venancio Flores and Manuel Herrera y Obes, for the government of Tomás Villalba, signed a peace accord at the Villa de la Unión. A general amnesty was granted to Blancos and Colorados, and Villalba handed the presidency to Flores.

title: Nobles, clergy and cities of Prussia form the Prussian Confederation
description: At Marienwerder, a group of 53 nobles and clergy and 19 cities in Prussia formed the Prussian Confederation to oppose the arbitrariness of the Teutonic Knights. It was based on the Lizard Union, set up by the nobles of Chełmno Land in 1397.

title: Pope Innocent IV grants the resignation of Thomas, Bishop of Finland
description: Thomas, the first known bishop of Finland, resigned after admitting, according to the pope, to felonies such as torturing a man to death and forging a papal letter. He lived his last years in the Dominican convent in Visby, Gotland, and died there in 1248.

title: Ferdinand of Majorca defeats Princess Matilda's forces at Picotin
description: The Catalan forces of Ferdinand of Majorca, claimant to Achaea, crushed the barons' levies and Burgundian knights loyal to Princess Matilda of Hainaut. Ferdinand was later killed by the troops of her husband, Louis of Burgundy, at Manolada.

title: Robert Stewart succeeds David II as King of Scots
description: David II died childless and was succeeded by his nephew Robert II, the first monarch of the House of Stuart. An armed protest by William, Earl of Douglas, delayed Robert's coronation until 26 March 1371.

title: Enslaved people rise on the Magdalenenberg plantation in Berbice
description: Enslaved people on plantation Magdalenenberg on the Canje River rebelled against harsh treatment and torched the plantation house; days later the revolt led by Cuffy began. Guyana marks 23 February as Republic Day in memory of the Berbice Rebellion.

title: Vandal king Huneric removes the Nicene bishops of his kingdom
description: After a meeting of Nicene and Arian bishops earlier that month, Huneric forcibly removed the Nicene bishops from office and banished some to Corsica. A few Nicenes who refused to become Arians were executed; his successor let the exiles return.

title: Nader Shah defeats the Mughal army of Muhammad Shah at Karnal
description: Nader Shah's forces defeated the army of the Mughal emperor Muhammad Shah within three hours near Karnal, 110 kilometres north of Delhi. The victory opened the way to the Iranian sack of Delhi and critically weakened the declining Mughal dynasty.

title: The three-year-old Guangxu Emperor ascends the Qing throne
description: Zaitian, a nephew of Cixi, took the throne aged three after the Tongzhi Emperor died without an heir, adopting the regnal name Guangxu, "continuation of splendor". The empress dowagers Ci'an and Cixi were his co-regents.

title: USS Ranger, the first US ship designed as a carrier, is launched
description: Ranger, the first US vessel designed and built from the keel up as an aircraft carrier, was launched at Newport News, Virginia. Commissioned in 1934, she spent most of World War II in the Atlantic and provided air support for Operation Torch.

title: Japan and Joseon Korea conclude a treaty opening Korean ports
description: Negotiations between the Empire of Japan and the Kingdom of Joseon were concluded. The treaty gave Japanese citizens extraterritoriality in Korea, opened three Korean ports to Japanese trade and ended Korea's status as a tributary state of Qing China.

title: Yuan Chonghuan is appointed Governor of Liaodong after Ningyuan
description: After his cannon-armed defence of Ningyuan halted Nurhaci's army, the Ming court made Yuan Chonghuan Governor of Liaodong, with full authority over all forces outside the passes. He later executed the general Mao Wenlong, making powerful enemies.

title: An Organic Act places the District of Columbia under Congress
description: The District of Columbia Organic Act formally placed the district under the control of the United States Congress and organized it into two counties, Washington and Alexandria. The charters of Georgetown and Alexandria were left in place.
source: District of Columbia Organic Act of 1801

title: The Fourth Council of Constantinople closes after ten sessions
description: The council, counted by the Catholic Church as the eighth ecumenical council, had met in Constantinople in ten sessions from October 869, with over 103 bishops, and issued 27 canons. A pro-Photian council of 879–80 was attended by 383 bishops.

title: A gun explodes aboard USS Princeton, killing the Secretary of State
description: During a Potomac River cruise for dignitaries, a gun exploded on the warship Princeton, killing six people, among them Secretary of State Abel P. Upshur and Navy Secretary Thomas Walker Gilmer. President John Tyler, below decks, was not injured.

title: Publius Valerius celebrates a triumph after the Battle of Silva Arsia
description: In what is traditionally the first year of the Republic, the consul Valerius brought the spoils of the battle against the deposed king Tarquin back to Rome and held a triumph. His four-horse chariot became the usual vehicle of a victorious Roman general.

title: Diocletian and Maximian name two Caesars, founding the Tetrarchy
description: At Milan Maximian gave Constantius the office of Caesar, and the same day Diocletian did the same for Galerius. The arrangement, called the Tetrarchy, "rulership by four", divided the empire's lands and implied a line of succession.

title: Skanderbeg gathers Albanian nobles in the League of Lezhë
description: Under Venetian patronage, Skanderbeg summoned Albanian noblemen to Lezhë, where they formed a military alliance against the Ottomans. It was the first time that much of Albania was united under a single leader, and his army fought the Ottomans until 1468.

title: King Vitiges and the Ostrogoths begin the siege of Rome
description: A numerically superior Ostrogothic army under Vitiges laid siege to Rome, held by Byzantine forces under Belisarius, who with his bucellarii was almost cut off outside the Flaminian Gate. The year-long siege shaped the rest of the Gothic War.

title: Akbar's Mughal army defeats the Bengal Sultanate at Tukaroi
description: The Mughal Empire defeated the army of Daud Khan Karrani, the last Sultan of Bengal, near the village of Tukaroi in present-day Odisha. The victory greatly weakened the Bengal Sultanate, whose rule ended in 1576.

title: A British force routs the Americans at Brier Creek in Georgia
description: A British force of 900 regulars and militia under Jacques Marcus Prevost defeated 1,100 Americans under John Ashe and Samuel Elbert; at least 150 Americans were killed and 227 captured. The battle boosted the Loyalist cause and damaged Patriot morale.

title: Ramathibodi I is established as sovereign of the Ayutthaya Kingdom
description: Having moved his capital that year to an island in the Chao Phraya River, where he founded Ayutthaya, Ramathibodi I was formally established as ruler of a centralized state. The city remained the kingdom's capital for over 400 years.

title: The Congregation of the Index suspends Copernicus's De revolutionibus
description: In connection with the Galileo affair, the Congregation of the Index suspended De revolutionibus until it could be "corrected", calling Copernicanism a "false Pythagorean doctrine". Corrections issued four years later treated heliocentrism as a hypothesis.

title: Spanish, Danish and US forces trap the pirate Roberto Cofresí
description: An alliance of Spain, the US West Indies Squadron and the Danish government of Saint Thomas forced Cofresí's sloop Anne into a 45-minute battle. He escaped overland but was ambushed and captured, and on 29 March he was executed by firing squad in San Juan.

title: Flanders gives up its claims on Zeeland in the Treaty of Paris
description: In the Treaty of Paris, Count Louis I of Flanders relinquished Flemish claims over the County of Zeeland and acknowledged William I, Count of Holland, as Count of Zeeland. William in turn renounced all claims on Flanders.

title: Sheikh Mujibur Rahman calls for a struggle for independence
description: At the Ramna Race Course, before over one million people and amid escalating tensions with West Pakistan, Mujib informally declared the independence of Bangladesh: "The struggle this time, is a struggle for our liberty." He announced civil disobedience.

title: Afghan Hotak forces defeat the Safavid army at Gulnabad
description: The army of the Hotak dynasty defeated the forces of the Safavid Empire at Gulnabad, further cementing the fall of a dynasty that had been declining for decades. Some historians date the end of Safavid Iran to 1722, when Isfahan fell to the Afghans.

title: Nader is crowned Shah of Iran after the assembly on the Moghan plain
description: Nader was crowned on a date his astrologers had chosen, before an assembly of the nobility, the military and religious elite and the Ottoman ambassador. He took the throne on terms that set up a dynasty in his name and accepted Sunni practices as legitimate.

title: Maximian makes a triumphal entry into Carthage after his Berber war
description: Having pressed deep into Berber territory, devastating land and driving the tribes back into the Sahara, Maximian entered Carthage in triumph. Inscriptions there hail him as redditor lucis aeternae, "restorer of the eternal light".

title: Bishop Tomás de Berlanga reaches the Galápagos Islands by chance
description: The bishop was sailing to Peru to settle a dispute between Francisco Pizarro and Diego de Almagro when the winds died and strong currents carried his ship out to the Galápagos Islands. He sent an account of the discovery to Charles V.

title: Arnošt of Pardubice is confirmed as the last Bishop of Prague
description: Arnošt of Pardubice, an advisor and diplomat to Charles IV, was confirmed bishop of Prague (3 March by the Julian calendar). The bishopric was raised to an archbishopric the next year, and he became its first archbishop.

title: The regent Theodora and her synod restore the icons to Hagia Sophia
description: After the death of the last iconoclast emperor, Theophilos, the regent Theodora and Patriarch Methodios led a procession from Blachernae to Hagia Sophia, restoring the icons. The synod decreed a yearly feast, the Sunday of Orthodoxy.

title: Spanish forces begin the siege of Maastricht in the Dutch Revolt
description: The siege of Maastricht, a battle of the Eighty Years' War between rebels in the Habsburg Netherlands and the Spanish government, began and lasted until 1 July. It ended in a Spanish victory.

title: Ignatius of Loyola and Francis Xavier are canonized as saints
description: Ignatius of Loyola, who with six companions had founded the Society of Jesus and was its first Superior General, was canonized together with Francis Xavier, the Jesuit co-founder who led the first Christian mission to Japan.

title: Muhammad defeats the Quraysh in the Battle of Badr
description: Near Badr, in present-day Saudi Arabia, Muhammad and an army of his Sahaba defeated a Quraysh army led by Amr ibn Hisham, known among Muslims as Abu Jahl. The battle, the Day of the Criterion in the Qur'an, began a six-year war between Muhammad and his tribe.

title: Felix III becomes Bishop of Rome after the death of Simplicius
description: Felix III was elected bishop of Rome following the death of Pope Simplicius earlier that month, and held the office until his death in 492. His repudiation of the Henotikon is considered the beginning of the Acacian schism.

title: Henry IV defeats the Catholic League and Spanish forces at Ivry
description: In the French Wars of Religion, Henry IV, leading French royal and English forces, won a decisive victory over the Catholic League under the Duke of Mayenne and Spanish forces under the Count of Egmont. He went on to lay siege to Paris.

title: France and Sweden force Bavaria into the Truce of Ulm
description: After French and Swedish armies invaded Bavaria, Mazarin signed a truce with Bavaria, Cologne and Sweden, and Maximilian I renounced his alliance with the emperor. The truce soon failed when the Bavarian general Johann von Werth refused to comply.

title: Al-Hadi ila'l-Haqq Yahya arrives in Sa'dah and founds a Zaydi imamate
description: Invited by tribal leaders to end the strife in northern Yemen, Yahya arrived in Sa'dah and soon proclaimed himself commander of the faithful as al-Hadi. The Zaydi imams of Yemen held power in parts of the country from then until 1970.

title: Constantius II raises his cousin Gallus to the rank of caesar
description: As he prepared to move against the usurper Magnentius, Constantius II needed a representative in the East and made Gallus caesar at Sirmium, giving him the name Constantius and his sister Constantina in marriage. Gallus set up residence in Antioch.

title: Over two hundred Cathars are burnt after the fall of Montségur
description: After a siege of the Cathar fortress of Montségur from May 1243, over 200 Cathar Perfects were burnt in an enormous pyre at the foot of the castle. Hunted by the Inquisition, the remaining Cathars became more and more scattered fugitives.

title: The Abenaki sagamore Samoset walks into Plymouth Colony
description: Samoset, an Abenaki sagamore, startled the colonists by walking into Plymouth Colony and greeting them in English: "Welcome, Englishmen." He was the first American Indian to make contact with the Pilgrims of the colony, founded the year before.

title: Marcus Aurelius dies, leaving Commodus as sole Roman emperor
description: Marcus Aurelius died on the Danubian front, leaving the 18-year-old Commodus as sole emperor. His sole reign is commonly thought to mark the end of the Pax Romana; Cassius Dio saw in it a descent "from a kingdom of gold to one of iron and rust".

title: Petronius Maximus takes the throne of the Western Roman Empire
description: With the support of the Senate, Maximus secured the throne after the murder of Valentinian III by paying palace officials, and married the reluctant widow Licinia Eudoxia. He reigned only 75 days before a mob killed him as the Vandals neared Rome.

title: Jacques de Molay, last Templar grand master, is burned at the stake
description: After he and Geoffroi de Charney retracted their confessions, calling the order pure and the charges fictitious, they were burned on the Ile des Juifs in the Seine. Henry Charles Lea gives this date; according to Alain Demurger, 11 March is more probable.

title: Zosimus becomes Bishop of Rome after the death of Innocent I
description: Zosimus succeeded Pope Innocent I, who had died on 12 March, and held the see until his death in December 418. He ruled for Arles in its dispute with Vienne over jurisdiction, and his fractious temper coloured all the controversies he joined.

title: Edward I issues the Statute of Rhuddlan for the conquered Welsh lands
description: Promulgated at Rhuddlan Castle after the conquest of Wales, the royal ordinance divided the principality into shires, among them Anglesey and Flintshire. It gave the constitutional basis for the government of the Principality of Wales until 1536.

skip: A single bank theft (burglars with copied keys, most of the money recovered): a crime of local note, trivial for a history site.

title: The Great Boston Fire destroys hundreds of buildings
description: A fire in Boston, in the Province of Massachusetts Bay, destroyed 349 buildings between the modern Washington Street and Fort Hill, as well as several ships in port. It left more than a thousand people homeless.

title: An earthquake destroys the city of Mendoza, Argentina
description: An earthquake with an estimated magnitude of 7.2 struck the province of Mendoza at 11:30 at night and destroyed its capital. It reached an intensity of IX–X on the Mercalli scale, from a hypocenter an estimated 30 kilometres deep.

title: The marriage of Louis VII and Eleanor of Aquitaine is annulled
description: The Council of Beaugency declared Louis VII and Eleanor too closely related for their marriage to be legal; in fact it owed more to their hostility and the lack of a male heir. Two months later Eleanor married the future Henry II of England.

title: Alexander H. Stephens delivers the Cornerstone Speech in Savannah
description: Alexander H. Stephens, acting Vice President of the Confederate States of America, gave the oration at the Athenaeum in Savannah, Georgia. He served as the only vice president of the Confederate States from 1861 to 1865.

title: The Minamoto defeat the Taira clan at the Battle of Yashima
description: In one of the battles of the Genpei War, fought in Sanuki Province on Shikoku, near present-day Takamatsu, the forces of the Taira clan were defeated by the Minamoto. The two were among the four clans that dominated Japanese politics in the Heian period.

title: George Washington signs the first US act against the slave trade
description: The law passed by Congress prohibited the building or outfitting of ships in US ports for the international slave trade. It was the first of several anti-slave-trade acts; in 1800 Congress strengthened it, sharply raising the fines.

title: Elisha Otis installs the first passenger safety elevator
description: Elisha Otis, who in 1853 had invented a device that stops an elevator from falling if the hoisting cable fails, installed the first safety elevator for passenger service in the store of E.V. Haughwout & Co. in New York City.

title: Stonewall Jackson opens his Valley campaign at Kernstown
description: The First Battle of Kernstown, in Frederick County and Winchester, Virginia, opened Stonewall Jackson's campaign through the Shenandoah Valley. Although a Confederate defeat, the engagement distracted Federal efforts to capture Richmond.

title: Rōnin assassinate the Tairō Ii Naosuke at the Sakurada Gate
description: Rōnin samurai of the Mito and Satsuma domains killed Ii Naosuke, Chief Minister of the Tokugawa shogunate, outside the Sakurada Gate of Edo Castle. He had held the post since 1858 and signed the Harris Treaty, opening ports to American trade.

title: Constantine becomes Bishop of Rome after the death of Sisinnius
description: Constantine, one of the last popes of the Byzantine Papacy, succeeded Pope Sisinnius. In 710/711 he visited Constantinople, where he compromised with Justinian II on the Trullan canons; the city's next papal visit came in 1967.

title: Amar Das becomes the third guru of Sikhism
description: Amar Das became Sikh Guru at the age of 73, the third of the gurus who established the religion over about two and a half centuries, a span beginning in 1469 with the birth of Guru Nanak, the founder of Sikhism.

title: Andrew Jackson defeats the Red Sticks at Horseshoe Bend
description: With an army of about 5,000, including Cherokee and pro-American Creek, Jackson defeated about a thousand Red Sticks, killing 800 of them. He then forced the Treaty of Fort Jackson on the Creek, who ceded most of western Georgia and part of Alabama to the US.

title: Mexican troops massacre Texian prisoners at Goliad
description: On the orders of Santa Anna, and despite appeals for clemency by General José de Urrea, 425–445 prisoners of war from the Texian Army were executed by the Mexican Army at Goliad. They had surrendered believing they would be set free within weeks.

title: British warships capture USS Essex off Valparaíso
description: Off Valparaíso, Chile, the frigate HMS Phoebe and the sloop HMS Cherub fought the frigate USS Essex and the sloop USS Essex Junior. The British ships won, and both American vessels were captured.
profile: United Kingdom of Great Britain and Ireland

title: Thomas Jefferson authorizes the Cumberland Road
description: Jefferson signed the act for a road from Cumberland, Maryland, to Ohio, the first great federally financed highway of the United States. By 1839 the National Road reached Vandalia, Illinois, 591 miles from Cumberland.

title: The Treaty of Saint-Germain-en-Laye returns New France to France
description: The treaty returned New France, Quebec among it, to French control after the English had seized the colony in 1629. It came after the Anglo-French War of 1627 to 1629 had ended, and the colony was again in French hands.

title: The United States organizes Florida as a territory
description: Florida, once the major part of the Spanish territory of La Florida and ceded to the United States in the 1819 Adams–Onís Treaty, became an organized incorporated territory. It was admitted to the Union as a state in 1845.

title: Dominican troops defeat the Haitian army at Santiago
description: In the second major battle of the Dominican War of Independence, outnumbered Dominican troops of the Army of the North under General José María Imbert defeated Haitian troops under General Jean-Louis Pierrot at Santiago de los Caballeros.

title: Matthew Perry and the Tokugawa shogunate sign the Convention of Kanagawa
description: Signed under threat of force, the treaty opened the ports of Shimoda and Hakodate to American vessels, effectively ending Japan's 220-year-old policy of national seclusion. Similar treaties with other Western powers followed.

title: American forces capture Malolos, capital of the Philippine Republic
description: The division of General Arthur MacArthur Jr. advanced along the Manila-Dagupan Railway and took Malolos, where the First Philippine Republic had been established. The Aguinaldo government had already moved its seat to San Isidro, Nueva Ecija.

title: The US House of Representatives meets for the first time
description: Less than a month after the Constitution took effect, the House convened in New York City, then the nation's capital, and elected Frederick Muhlenberg of Pennsylvania as its first speaker. Under the Great Compromise, its seats were divided by population.

title: Alexios Komnenos seizes Constantinople from Nikephoros III
description: After bribing the Western troops guarding the city, Isaac and Alexios Komnenos entered the capital, overthrowing Nikephoros III Botaneiates. Alexios was crowned on 4 April after his troops had looted Constantinople for three days.

title: Honorius IV is elected pope unanimously on the first ballot
description: Honorius IV was chosen after the death of Martin IV, the last French pope to hold his court in Rome before the move to Avignon. His papacy, which lasted until 1287, fell in a tumultuous period of political strife and conflict in Sicily.

title: Cree warriors kill nine people at Frog Lake
description: In the Cree uprising of the North-West Rebellion, Cree men led by Wandering Spirit attacked the small settlement of Frog Lake, in the District of Saskatchewan of the North-West Territories, and killed nine officials, clergy and settlers.

title: Henry IV grants Friuli to the Patriarch of Aquileia
description: Emperor Henry IV granted the county of Friuli, with ducal status, to Sigaerd, Patriarch of Aquileia, founding the patriarchal state of Friuli. It became one of the best organized polities of the Italian Middle Ages and lasted until 1420.

title: McClellan's Union army begins the siege of Yorktown
description: Marching up the Peninsula from Fort Monroe toward Richmond, George B. McClellan's Army of the Potomac met John B. Magruder's small Confederate force behind the Warwick Line at Yorktown and settled in for a siege, which lasted until 4 May.

title: Dutch nobles present the Compromise petition to Margaret of Parma
description: Two hundred noblemen led by Hendrick van Brederode forced their way to the regent Margaret of Parma with a petition seeking to moderate the placards against heresy. The petition played a crucial role in the events leading to the Dutch Revolt.

title: Stilicho defeats Alaric and the Visigoths at Pollentia
description: During the first Gothic invasion of Italy, the Romans under Stilicho defeated the Visigoths under Alaric I and forced him to retreat. Alaric was beaten again at Verona the next year and left Italy until his second invasion in 409, after the death of Stilicho.

title: Joseph Smith formally organizes the Church of Christ in New York
description: The Latter Day Saint church founded by Joseph Smith, informally organized in 1829 in upstate New York, was formally organized at Fayette or Manchester. It was the first body to follow the principles of his newly published Book of Mormon.

title: Attila and his army capture Metz
description: Marching west into Belgica with Gepids, Ostrogoths, Alans and other vassals, Attila captured Metz, killing most of its people and burning the town; he also took Strasbourg. Aëtius and the Visigoths later checked him at the Catalaunian Plains.

title: Ayutthaya falls to the Burmese, ending the Siamese kingdom
description: Burmese troops entered through tunnels under the walls, massacred inhabitants and burned palaces and temples, ending the 417-year-old Ayutthaya Kingdom. About 30,000 Siamese were taken to Burma; Taksin later moved the royal seat to Thonburi.

title: The Mongols reach the walls of Kaifeng, capital of the Jin
description: Two armies sent by Ögedei Khan, one led by himself and one by his brother Tolui, converged under Subutai and began the siege of Kaifeng, the capital of the Jurchen-led Jin dynasty. The city fell in 1233, and the Jin were conquered in 1234.
source: Mongol conquest of the Jin dynasty

title: The Venetian Republic and Milan make peace at Lodi
description: Signed in the city of Lodi, the peace agreement ended the Wars in Lombardy between the Venetian Republic and the Duchy of Milan. It established a balance of power among the northern Italian city-states that lasted almost 50 years.

title: Leo IV becomes pope after the death of Sergius II
description: Leo IV succeeded Sergius II, whose pontificate had seen the Arab raid against Rome. Leo repaired the churches damaged in the raid, built the Leonine Wall around Vatican Hill and organized a league of Italian cities that won the sea Battle of Ostia.

title: Adeodatus II becomes pope after the death of Vitalian
description: Adeodatus II, a Benedictine monk of Sant'Erasmo al Celio in Rome, succeeded Vitalian. He devoted much of his papacy to improving churches and fighting monothelitism, and rejected the synodical letters of the Patriarch of Constantinople.

title: Costa Rican militia defeat William Walker at the Second Battle of Rivas
description: Costa Rican militia under General Juan Rafael Mora Porras fought the Nicaraguan forces of the American mercenary William Walker. The drummer Juan Santamaría died carrying a torch to set the enemy stronghold on fire, and became the national hero of Costa Rica.

title: Shapur I is crowned co-ruler of the Sasanian Empire
description: Ardashir I, founder of the Sasanian Empire, had named Shapur his successor in a council of the magnates, and Shapur was crowned co-ruler with him. He may have been crowned again as sole ruler in 243, but Richard N. Frye thinks a single coronation more likely.

title: Union raiders seize the locomotive General in the Andrews Raid
description: Union volunteers led by the civilian scout James J. Andrews commandeered the locomotive The General at Big Shanty, Georgia, and took it north toward Chattanooga, damaging the Western and Atlantic Railroad. Confederate forces chased them for 87 miles.

title: Saladin crushes the Zengids at the Horns of Hama
description: Heavily outnumbered, Saladin took the hills by the Orontes and surrounded the attacking armies of Mosul and Aleppo. Victory gave him Damascus, Homs and Hama; he then proclaimed himself king, and the Abbasid caliph named him Sultan of Egypt and Syria.
